counterfactual_missing_items: R3 lacks raw CK elevation and myoglobinuria spans, capturing only the downstream ATN finding
R6 lacks raw ATN/muddy brown cast and myoglobinuria spans, so it cannot identify the cause of AKI
R4 has no supplied raw supporting span and only appears as a late complication
decisive_items: Urine sediment showed acute tubular necrosis with muddy brown casts
response.rationale: R1 uniquely integrates elevated CK, myoglobinuria, and muddy brown cast ATN into one causal chain of rhabdomyolysis causing ATN/AKI. R3 names only the ATN sediment finding, while R6 only captures creatinine elevation; R4 is a downstream arrhythmia with no primary explanatory raw support.

rejected.why: AKI is a downstream syndrome supported mainly by creatinine/oliguria and lacks the specific muscle-injury and ATN-sediment evidence that identifies rhabdomyolysis as the cause.
Its supplied raw support is empty; rapid atrial fibrillation is a complication and does not explain the CK elevation, myoglobinuria, or ATN.
